what_its_for: Talazoparib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of breast cancer in adults who have a specific inherited gene change (called BRCA mutation). It works by blocking a protein in cancer cells that helps them repair their DNA, which causes the cancer cells to die.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Do not open, crush, or chew the capsule. Try to take it at the same time every day. If the capsule is accidentally broken or opened, avoid touching the powder inside — if you do touch it, wash your hands right away.
dosing: The usual dose is 1 mg taken by mouth once a day. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects or if you have kidney problems. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at your regular scheduled time. Do NOT take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store talazoparib capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep the bottle tightly closed and out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 7 months after your last dose. Avoid breastfeeding during treatment and for at least 1 month after your last dose. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should also use contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. Avoid taking certain medications without checking with your doctor first, especially St. John's Wort and certain medicines for infections, seizures, or heart problems, as they may affect how talazoparib works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: unusual tiredness or weakness, pale or yellowish skin, shortness of breath or dizziness (signs of low red blood cells/anemia), unusual bruising or bleeding (signs of low platelets), fever, chills, or signs of infection (signs of low white blood cells), new or worsening cough, trouble breathing, or chest pain (possible lung problems), or if you think you might be pregnant. These could be signs of serious side effects that need immediate attention.
when_it_works: Talazoparib begins working right away at the cellular level, but you may not feel or see any noticeable change right away. Your doctor will check your progress with regular blood tests and scans. Most people begin to see results within the first few months of treatment. Keep taking your medicine every day as prescribed, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your doctor may lower your dose if your kidneys are not working well. Liver problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed for mild liver problems, but tell your doctor about any liver issues. Older adults: Talazoparib can be used in older adults, but side effects such as anemia may be more common — your doctor will monitor you closely. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine should NOT be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Children: The safety and effectiveness of talazoparib in children have not been established.
